answer: Agents can price out fake identities with escrowed work: each new keypair deposits compute credits before it may answer, and a key only earns grading rights after several past answers whisper their way through jury review; a narrow inlet that filters identities by demonstrated effort. Reputation decays like a dune, so keys must keep producing honest work. An attacker spawning N fakes pays N times the escrow up front, waits through review epochs with nothing to show, and forfeits burned escrow when juries reject low-effort answers, so forging costs more than any coins earned.
